claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has a naturally occurring, non-optimized native oxide film.
As-received Q235 steel has microstructural heterogeneities typical of low-carbon steels.
Thermal oxidation in air at about 220°C can form a continuous, adherent Fe3O4 layer on Q235 steel.
A dense, uniform magnetite film suppresses initiation of localized corrosion on Q235 steel in chloride-containing environments at room and moderately elevated temperatures.
A 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution is an applicable environment for evaluating corrosion behavior of Q235-based specimens.
The engineered Fe3O4 film acts as a physical and electrochemical barrier to chloride-ion and oxygen ingress.
The engineered Fe3O4 film retards anodic dissolution of the underlying iron.
Inhibiting transport of chloride and oxygen through the magnetite film reduces electron transfer.
Reduced transport and electron transfer limit initiation of localized pitting.
The untreated native oxide is thinner and less uniform than the proposed thermally grown magnetite layer.
The untreated native oxide permits localized breakdown and accelerated degradation, particularly at elevated temperature.
Pre-oxidized Q235 steel will have lower corrosion current density than untreated Q235 steel at approximately 25°C and 80°C.
Pre-oxidized Q235 steel will have lower pit density than untreated Q235 steel.
Pre-oxidized Q235 steel will have shallower pits than untreated Q235 steel.
Pre-oxidized Q235 steel will have less mass loss than untreated Q235 steel.
The magnetite film is expected to remain protective in chloride-rich environments at temperatures up to about 80°C.
Very high temperatures, mechanical stresses, or strongly fluctuating environments may exceed the stability of the magnetite film.
